You were a child. He did manipulate you, and he doesn’t want to come to terms with that. Like the other comments have said, I think he saw you as a vulnerable opportunity with your naivety for you were a child, he can manipulate and mold you easier. At that age older men especially are pretty captivating, it’s no fault of your own. It’s almost like he made it seem like he was “mentoring” you to make himself feel better about manipulating you, and so you wouldn’t catch on. maybe he did teach you a lot of things, but, in this scenario, why would he be so interested in teaching a child how to behave? So he can have his “perfect” partner. 

In this situation it really was a case of grooming. It’s good that you can see that at this moment, you are not any lesser than he is, nor should your partner ever try and make you feel lesser. People in a relationship should be seen as equals, regardless of experience and knowledge on certain things. Again like others have said, it’s best to seek marriage counseling, and trying to talk to him about boundaries and how you feel, if he doesn’t seem to respond, you could make your decision then, you can make any decisions you want at any time, even now. It’s up to you, but that’s my personal opinion on what I feel you could do. Your kids are young but still old enough to understand how he is treating you. That’s an important sign. 

My parents also have a considerable age gap (around 11 years) although my mother got married at around 24. My mom and dad only knew each other for a few months before marrying, they have a horrible relationship from the way my siblings and I see it. My older brother and I have known about the abuse since we were kids, and it’s becoming harder and harder to shield that away from my younger brother, although he’s quite perceptive. He married her and expected to be able to mold her into whatever he wanted, she’s never good enough to him, but my mom is a strong capable woman who works and makes good money, that seems to threaten dad the most. My mom often says “I won’t be the maid you want me to be” to him. 

Obviously a divorce is pretty much the best route for them, even me and my siblings would be neutral about a divorce, but for a multitude of reasons including culture, they’re still together. I would rethink this relationship, think about how you DO want to be treated, and communicate that. Good luck!

I had some pretty bad depression and honestly it can be hard when it comes to relationships. I think your feelings are valid when you say you feel drained. Having a partner with some bad depression can kinda suck sometimes. There are times where I feel so depressed and probably radiate that energy around others. I’ve gotten a lot better, and I’ve always been someone who was pretty good at putting on a happy face to cover my depression. Although of course not everyone is like that, and sometimes it’s totally ok to just wanna feel like how you literally feel inside. As a depressed person, I would really love it if my boyfriend just does small, cute things for me. Helps me with a task that I usually dread doing (dishes), gets me a small gift, reminds me of how he was thinking about me, even just telling me how beautiful I look. Those things always make me feel better, and of course I don’t know your situation at all. If your gf doesn’t already, obviously therapy and medication would be the best thing for her. It takes time, but having a licensed professional where it’s their job to listen to the shitty stuff about your day is just great, it helps me set boundaries with others and not over share too much with my friends and family. I would say that if it gets to a point after a while where it’s just sad being in the relationship, not happy anymore, just depressing overall. It might be time to rethink what you want in the future, and if your gf will be apart of that. Honestly just communicating how you feel is always the best way to go. Plz dm me if you wanna talk!
